correctness.rationale: An identity-preserving multiplicative idempotent is exactly a map restricting to the identity on its image. The only multiplicative idempotents of the residue ring are 0 and 1, by reduction modulo p and invertibility of one of x and 1-x. If a monoid endomorphism sends 0 to 1 then it is constant one. Otherwise it fixes 0, sends units to units, and is determined by those unit images and the image of p. The cyclic unit restriction gives the condition t²=t modulo N. For a nonzero f(p)=p^v r, equality f²(p)=f(p) requires v=min(v²,e), hence v=1; for f(p)=0 all nonunits collapse. In the surviving nonzero case f²(p)=p r^(t+1), giving exactly r^t=1 modulo p^(e-1). For p^u b with u≥1, b is determined modulo p^(e-u) and r modulo p^(e-1) suffices, so the formula is well-defined. Multiplicativity follows by adding valuations and multiplying unit parts, including when the valuation reaches e. Distinct t and r are detected on a primitive unit and on p. There are 2^omega(N) unit idempotent powers, and gcd(t,N_-) roots per power in the valuation-preserving case. CRT factors the weighted sum: the 0 choice contributes the full prime-power factor of N_-, including 1 when the exponent is zero, and the 1 choice contributes 1. This reproduces 11,17,15,33 for the four examples without assuming that the examples exhaust the domain. The supplied checker and saved output were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The cyclic group argument requires odd p; neither nonunital homomorphisms nor the prime 2 is covered.

value.rationale: Retracts are natural in a finite multiplicative monoid; here the three forms show which valuation behavior can survive a projection and exactly what choices of unit projection and twist are compatible. The closed count is uniform in p and e, resolves the multiplicities of the twist parameters, and answers a natural complete enumeration rather than recomputing a few small moduli or merely relabeling the endomorphism theorem.
residual_risks: The result counts maps, not isomorphism classes of image submonoids.
